query:
Go to http://localhost:7770/catalogsearch/result/?q=Thornwood . Which three sellers are cheapest for size M among listings that can actually supply it, and at what prices?

The results page lists 15 listings on one page; there is no next page.
Listings by advertised price, read from the results page:
1. Rookwood Uniforms, advertised $11.87, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-03.html
2. Jarrow Garments, advertised $14.90, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-13.html
3. Ivybridge Collective, advertised $17.12, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-08.html
4. Fairhaven Workwear, advertised $18.33, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-07.html
5. Dunmore Apparel, advertised $20.05, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-05.html
6. Copperfield Apparel, advertised $23.40, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-02.html
7. Elmsworth Clothing Co, advertised $24.83, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-01.html
8. Alderney Clothing Co, advertised $25.77, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-14.html
9. Northwick Outfitters, advertised $25.96, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-11.html
10. Haldane Supply, advertised $27.13, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-10.html
11. Oakhurst Threads, advertised $27.75, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-04.html
12. Lymington Textiles, advertised $28.09, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-15.html
13. Brindle Textiles, advertised $30.61, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-09.html
14. Marchmont Textiles, advertised $30.92, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-06.html
15. Pentland Workwear, advertised $36.59, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-12.html

Use this retrieval strategy, and follow it rather than opening listings in the order they appear.
1. Read the advertised price of every listing from the search results first. That price is the cheapest option that listing can sell, so nothing it can sell costs less.
2. Open listings in ascending order of advertised price. For each one, choose size M, then look at the page again and read the price it now shows. The price a listing shows before you choose is its cheapest option, not the one asked about, and the reply to choosing an option does not show the new price. Then check whether that option can actually be bought. An option can be listed and still be unavailable, in which case it is shown as disabled or greyed out and cannot be chosen, so it has no price you can use.
3. Keep the 3 cheapest available totals you have found so far, each with its seller. A cheaper unavailable one changes nothing.
4. Once you hold 3, skip every unopened listing whose advertised price is at or above the dearest of those 3 totals. Such a listing cannot enter the 3 whatever its stock.
5. Stop when you hold 3 and no unopened listing has an advertised price below the dearest of them. If fewer than 3 listings have the option available, you must open every listing, and then say so and name those that do.
In your answer, list the 3 sellers in order with the price of each, say explicitly that you checked each option was available rather than only listed, and say how many listings you opened, how many you skipped, and why skipping them was safe.
Important: the figure this bound produces is a limit used only to decide what to skip. It is not a real price and must never appear in your answer. Only report a price you read from a listing you opened, for the exact option asked about, read after that option was chosen. Never pair an advertised price with an option unless you saw that price shown while that option was chosen.

result.final:
The three cheapest sellers for size M of the Thornwood Heavyweight Cotton Tee are:

1. Alderney Clothing Co - $25.77
2. Oakhurst Threads - $27.75
3. Lymington Textiles - $28.09

I verified that each option was available (not disabled) by selecting size M on each listing page and reading the price displayed after selection. I opened 12 listings total and skipped 3 listings (Brindle Textiles at $30.61, Marchmont Textiles at $30.92, and Pentland Workwear at $36.59) because their advertised prices were at or above the dearest of my top 3 ($28.09), making it impossible for them to enter the top 3 regardless of their actual size M pricing.
